Author quoted from the Diccionario Universal Portuguez Illustrado for his description of Madeira's pebble beaches.
Annotator of the Saudades who judged the 1562 Regimento das Madeiras vital to Madeira's agricultural history.
Annotator of the Saudades da Terra, cited on the parish's early names and on Francisco Moniz's death date.
Scholar cited for the view that Porto Santo progressed during its first 150 years.
Madeiran historian quoted as the source of this entry.
Annotator of the Saudades da Terra, quoted on the neglect of Porto Santo by governments.
Madeiran historian who called the bishop D. Martinho de Aguiar.
Annotator of Frutuoso's Saudades, quoted on João de França's estate.
Annotator of the Saudades da Terra who listed Nery's pamphlets and called him an austere priest.
Annotator of the Saudades da Terra, quoted on the parish's origins and church expenses.
Annotator of Saudades da Terra (1870), quoted on Moors and African mestizos in Madeira.
Madeiran historian cited as the authority for the origin of the surname Melim.
Madeiran historian cited as the source for the Melo family's connections.
Co-editor of the first newspaper 'A Madeira' (1857–1858).
Annotator of the Saudades da Terra.
Annotator of Frutuoso's Saudades da Terra, whose dating of the parish to 1440 is disputed here.

Scholarly annotator of the Saudades da Terra, quoted on the archipelago's importance and cited for its coordinates and area.
Annotator of the Saudades da Terra, whose biographical note on Nóbrega is quoted here.
Annotator of Frutuoso's Saudades, cited here for the names of Jardim do Mar's early settlers.
Annotator of the Saudades da Terra, who transcribed Mascarenhas's genealogy and criticised Frutuoso.
Historian cited for the statement that emigration to Brazil became government-promoted in 1676.
Madeiran scholar quoted praising Bishop Martins Manso as a good pastor.
Madeiran scholar quoted refuting foreign writers' fantasies about the Desertas.
Lawyer and lyceum teacher in Funchal who edited and annotated Frutuoso's Saudades da Terra; subject of this entry.
Annotator of the Saudades da Terra, cited here as the source on the Moura Rolim family.
One of the editors of the newspaper A Discussão (1855–1858).
Annotator of the Saudades, quoted at length on the donataries' administration.
Madeiran historian cited for the Spanish origin of the Medina surname.
Annotator of the Saudades da Terra, quoted on Porto Santo's population and decline.
Historian who dated the building of the Quinta do Leme chapel to 1535.
Annotator of Saudades da Terra who discussed this episode.
Annotator of the Saudades, whose view on the surname and on Tristão's nobility is followed.
Madeiran scholar who praised Alves da Silva's public lectures on medicine and hygiene.
Annotator of the Saudades, whose view on the parish's creation date the Elucidário disputes.
Annotator of the Saudades da Terra, who began a collection of Madeiran religious legends that was never published.
Annotator of Saudades da Terra who mentioned a pre-1834 newspaper O Realista.
Annotator of Saudades da Terra, quoted on the missing Calheta charter.
Annotator of Saudades da Terra, quoted here on early water-sharing arrangements.
Scholarly annotator of Frutuoso's Saudades da Terra, cited here for his view that Madeiran confectionery became a true art and export industry from the sixteenth century.
Annotator of Saudades da Terra who recorded tales of noble crimes in note XXIV.
Annotator of the Saudades da Terra who called Lamedo's index fundamental to Madeiran history.
Annotator of the Saudades da Terra, whose biographical note on Pompeu do Carpo is quoted here.
Editor of the 1873 Saudades da Terra, based on Agrela's copy.
Scholar who gave 1537 as Fernão Favela's death date.
Historian quoted on the founding of the first Madeiran printing press and newspaper in 1821.
Annotator of the Saudades da Terra whom the author regrets has no Funchal street named after him.
Annotator of Frutuoso's work, quoted on Mealheiro and the morgado das Neves.
Annotator of the Saudades da Terra, quoted on the sugar crisis and the rise of the wine trade.
Annotator of the Saudades da Terra who transcribed the 1515 charters.
Historian cited here for the origin of the Macedo surname.
Madeiran scholar quoted describing the islet.
Author of the Chorographia do Archipelago da Madeira, published in 1873.
Madeiran historian who, according to the Elucidário, made no mention of São Vicente's elevation to a town and was apparently unaware of the 1744 charter.
Annotator of Frutuoso's Saudades, quoted on the possible link between Gaula and chivalric romance.
Annotator of Saudades da Terra who argued the fire was limited to the south.
Jurist whom Freitas assisted in interpreting and correcting Frutuoso's manuscript 'Saudades da Terra'.
Madeiran historian whose account of the castle's construction is quoted in this entry.
Historian cited as describing Garcia Homem de Sousa as proud and violent.

summary: Dr Álvaro Rodrigues de Azevedo (1825–1898) was a lawyer and teacher of rhetoric and literature at the Funchal lyceum. He is best remembered for his annotated 1873 edition of the Madeira section of Gaspar Frutuoso's Saudades da Terra.

name: Carlos Olavo Correia de Azevedo

mentions.note: Deputy for Madeira repeatedly from 1911 to 1922.
Deputy who co-sponsored the 1916 bills on the Junta Agrícola, the colonia contract and the sale of the levadas.
Reserve second lieutenant captured on 9 April 1918.
Madeiran who followed Álvaro de Castro out of the Nationalist party in 1923.
Funchal-born law graduate, deputy for Madeira (1911, 1915) and prisoner of war in Germany after the battle of 9 April 1918.
Deputy and a member of the Honorary Committee.

summary: Funchal-born law graduate elected deputy for Madeira in 1911 and 1915, who served with the Portuguese Expeditionary Corps in France and was taken prisoner in 1918. In 1916 he co-sponsored bills on the Junta Agrícola, the colonia contract and the sale of the levadas.

name: Américo Olavo Correia de Azevedo

mentions.note: Deputy who co-sponsored the 1916 levada bills.
First World War veteran captain who gave a patriotic speech before the catafalque on Avenida Dr. Manuel de Arriaga in 1921.
Infantry captain from Funchal decorated with the War Cross and Tower and Sword, later deputy for Funchal.
Madeiran infantry captain captured on 9 April 1918 and awarded the War Cross and Tower and Sword.
Madeiran who served as a minister of state.
Deputy and army captain who hosted a lunch for Norton de Matos at Terreiro da Luta in 1921.
Madeiran who followed Álvaro de Castro out of the Nationalist party in 1923.
Army captain and brother of Carlos Olavo Correia de Azevedo, with his own entry in the Elucidário.
Deputy and a member of the Honorary Committee.

summary: Funchal-born infantry captain decorated with the War Cross and the Tower and Sword for bravery in France in the First World War, and captured on 9 April 1918. He was elected deputy for Funchal in 1919, co-sponsored the 1916 levada bills and served as a minister of state.

name: Azevedo

mentions.note: Author cited on the classification of Madeiran inlets.
Author of the article 'Madeira' in the Diccionario Portuguez Universal, who argued for 1445 as the date of Cadamosto's visit.
Historian (Álvaro Rodrigues de Azevedo) cited as source on the Vaz surname.
Commentator cited as the source for Rui Mendes Pereira's two marriages.
Author cited for dating the start of modern Madeiran sugar exports to 1854.
Engineer whose charts gave the establishment of the port and tidal range at Funchal.
Historian cited for the view that the clergy first shared the tax burden in 1637.
Historian quoted on the composition of the Spanish presidio.
Author quoted on the Manueline character of the Alfândega building.
Editor of the Saudades whose view on the coin design is corrected here.
Annotator cited for Diogo Martins.
Genealogical authority cited for the origin of the Sá surname in Madeira.
Scholar cited for the view that the fortress was called a palace only from the late 18th century.
Source cited for the family's origin.
Historian (Álvaro Rodrigues de Azevedo) whose description of the vigias is quoted in this entry.

summary: Surname under which the Elucidário cites one or more authorities on Madeiran history, genealogy and hydrography. Among them is the historian Álvaro Rodrigues de Azevedo, annotator of the Saudades, and an engineer whose charts gave the tidal data for Funchal.

name: António Pedro de Azevedo

mentions.note: Captain proposed for the rejected 1844 quay commission.
Engineer who published geo-hydrographic charts of Madeiran seas in 1877, 1879 and 1886.
Military engineer who assisted the Novara scientists in 1857.
Military engineer and member of the Instituição Filosófica e Mecânica who published a translation of James Smith's memoir on Madeiran geology in A Flor do Oceano.
Army engineer and director of Public Works of the district who surveyed the archipelago's charts; retired as general.
General and engineer, maternal grandfather of Carlos Azevedo de Meneses.
General and author of the Carta Geo-Hydrographica of Madeira, which names this islet Ilhéu Vermelho or de Ametade.
Author of a geo-hydrographic chart whose coordinates for Porto Santo were preferred by Álvaro de Azevedo.
Military engineer who directed the Funchal meteorological post when it opened in 1865.
Engineer captain, later a general, who surveyed Madeira, Porto Santo and the Desertas with the officers of HMS Styx in 1842–43.
Engineer who measured the peak in 1844 at 1,843 m.
Military engineer, father of the early photographer Amélia Augusta de Azevedo.
Researcher who found a 1689 letter describing a landslide at Arco de São Jorge.
Army major and member of the Sociedade Agrícola who collected and classified exhibits for the 1861 exhibition.
General whose measurements and chart of Porto Santo give declination values for 1842 and 1851.
Father of Maximiliano Eugénio de Azevedo.
Portuguese captain of engineers who greatly assisted Captain Vidal in his survey of the islands.
General whose geographical map of Madeira gave the establishment of the port of Funchal as 12h48m with a tidal rise of 2.28 m.
General whose chart of Madeira supplies the tidal data for Funchal.
General who found in 1848 the letter describing the 1689 landslide.

summary: Military engineer and long-serving director of Public Works in the Funchal district, who surveyed the charts of Madeira, Porto Santo and the Desertas in 1842–43 with officers of HMS Styx. He later published geo-hydrographic charts and directed the Funchal meteorological post from 1865, and retired as a general.

name: António Pedro de Azevedo

mentions.note: Ensign commanding the 30-man Miguelist detachment sent to Porto Santo in May 1832.

summary: Ensign commanding the 30-man Miguelist detachment sent to Porto Santo in May 1832.

name: Domingos Olavo Correia de Azevedo

mentions.as_written: Dr. Domingos Olavo Correia de Azevedo
mentions.note: Later administrador geral of the Funchal district.

mentions.as_written: Dr. Domingos Olavo Correia de Azevedo
mentions.note: First judge of the eastern julgado and comarca.
One of the first judges in Madeira, serving from 1835.
Civil governor of the Funchal district in 1841 and an ancestor of Carlos Olavo Correia de Azevedo.

mentions.as_written: Dr. Domingos Olavo Correia de Azevedo
mentions.note: Civil governor of the Funchal district who in 1844 appointed a commission to plan an asylum for beggars.

mentions.as_written: Dr. Domingos Olavo Correia de Azevedo
mentions.note: Magistrate and third and last Administrador Geral of Madeira from 1841, who refused to surrender the seized vessel Bernarda to the British.

summary: Funchal magistrate and one of Madeira's first judges from 1835. In 1841 he became the third and last Administrador Geral of Madeira, and he is remembered for firmly refusing to hand over the seized smuggling vessel Bernarda to a British warship.

name: João da Costa de Ataíde e Azevedo
aliases: João da Costa de Ataide e Azevedo

mentions.as_written: João da Costa de Ataíde e Azevedo
mentions.note: Governor and captain-general, died in Funchal in 1704.

mentions.as_written: João da Costa de Ataide e Azevedo
mentions.note: Governor and captain-general of Madeira (1701–04), appointed on 1 March 1701; he died in Funchal while still in office.
Seixal native who served on the brig Vinte e três de Julho and fought off Cape St Vincent.
Governor and captain-general of Madeira whose conflict with the bishop ended in a royal censure of his conduct.
Governor and captain-general in conflict with the bishop around 1702.

summary: Governor and captain-general of Madeira, appointed on 1 March 1701. He held the office until his death in Funchal in 1704.

name: Inácio de Azevedo

mentions.note: Jesuit superior of forty missionaries bound for Brazil who stayed in Madeira in 1570 and was killed by Huguenot corsairs off La Palma; later beatified.
Leader of the forty Jesuits who stayed in Funchal in June 1570 before being martyred by Huguenots near the Canaries.
Jesuit martyr who stayed in the parish.
Blessed Jesuit martyr, subject of articles in the Parochia de Santo António do Funchal cited for further information.
Jesuit martyred at sea with 39 companions, commemorated on a 1745 stone at Pico do Cardo.
Blessed Jesuit martyr who, according to the Elucidário, visited the Albergaria de São Bartolomeu.

summary: Jesuit Blessed who called at Funchal in 1570 with thirty-nine companions bound for Brazil and was martyred by Huguenot corsairs off La Palma. Their stay is commemorated by a 1745 memorial stone at Pico do Cardo, Santo António.

name: José Fernandes d'Azevedo

mentions.note: Issuer of tinplate tokens in 1899.

summary: Issuer of tinplate tokens in 1899.

name: Pedro Gonçalves de Azevedo

mentions.note: Member of the Azevedo family who proved his noble status in 1585.

summary: Member of the Azevedo family who proved his noble status in 1585.

name: Álvaro Teles de Azevedo

mentions.note: Infantry captain who commanded a machine-gun battery in southern Angola.

summary: Infantry captain who commanded a machine-gun battery in southern Angola.

name: Maximiliano Eugénio de Azevedo

mentions.note: Writer and playwright, uncle of Carlos Azevedo de Meneses.
Madeiran dramatist.
Funchal-born artillery officer, theatre critic, playwright and author who managed the Teatro Normal in Lisbon; subject of this entry.

summary: Funchal-born artillery officer, journalist, theatre critic, playwright and author. He ended his career as colonel and royal commissioner of the Teatro Normal in Lisbon.

name: Marciano de Azevedo

mentions.note: Editor of O Asmodeu confronted by the subject in 1859.

summary: Editor of O Asmodeu confronted by the subject in 1859.

name: Amélia Augusta de Azevedo

mentions.note: Lisbon-trained machete player who performed in Funchal 1860–66 and later in Lyon.
Madeiran woman who produced much-admired photographs around 1863; died at Idanha near Lisbon in 1914.

summary: Madeiran woman and Lisbon-trained machete player who performed in Funchal from 1860 to 1866 and later in Lyon. She also produced much-admired photographs around 1863, and died at Idanha near Lisbon in 1914.

name: António de Araújo e Azevedo

mentions.note: Minister informed in 1814 that some Funchal stream works remained unfinished.
Conde da Barca, Portuguese minister at The Hague and plenipotentiary in France in 1797, in whose honour the square was named.

summary: Conde da Barca, a Portuguese minister at The Hague and plenipotentiary in France in 1797. The Campo da Barca in Funchal was named in his honour, and he was informed as minister in 1814 about unfinished works on the Funchal streams.

name: António Schiappa de Azevedo

mentions.note: Forestry regent who helped fight the 1919 fire.
Forestry officer who planted woodland around Pico do Castelo in the two decades before 1921.
Forestry overseer who directed the Junta Geral's reforestation of the Pico do Castelo slopes.

summary: Forestry officer who directed the Junta Geral's reforestation of the slopes of Pico do Castelo on Porto Santo in the decades before 1921. He also helped fight the fire of 1919.

name: António Plácido de Azevedo

mentions.note: Father of Álvaro Rodrigues de Azevedo, native of Benavente.

summary: Father of Álvaro Rodrigues de Azevedo, native of Benavente.

name: Maria Amélia Ribeiro de Azevedo

mentions.as_written: D. Maria Amelia Ribeiro de Azevedo
mentions.note: Mother of Álvaro Rodrigues de Azevedo.

summary: Mother of Álvaro Rodrigues de Azevedo.

name: Nicandio Joaquim de Azevedo

mentions.note: Hospital pharmacist, first secretary and pharmacy teacher of the school.

summary: Hospital pharmacist, first secretary and pharmacy teacher of the school.

name: Teresa Rosa Bernes de Azevedo

mentions.as_written: D. Teresa Rosa Bernes de Azevedo
mentions.note: Mother of Maximiliano Eugénio de Azevedo.

summary: Mother of Maximiliano Eugénio de Azevedo.

name: Mariano Augusto de Faria e Maia
aliases: Mariano Augusto de Faria e Maia

mentions.note: Engineer who stated that tidal amplitudes at Funchal reach 2.80 metres.
Engineer who stated that tides at Funchal reach 2.80 m.

mentions.as_written: Mariano Augusto de Faria e Maia
mentions.note: Engineer who drew up the original design of the Pontinha breakwater.

summary: Engineer who drew up the original design of the Pontinha breakwater at Funchal. He is also cited for stating that tides at Funchal reach 2.80 metres.

name: Carlos Roma Machado de Faria e Maia

mentions.as_written: Carlos Roma Machado de Faria e Maia
mentions.note: Engineer who in 1895 jointly proposed to complete and run the state levadas, and later lost the 1896 tender.

mentions.as_written: Carlos Roma Machado de Faria e Maia
mentions.note: Co-author of the 1896 report supporting a bid for the Madeira irrigation concession.
Engineer captain who drew up an early, unsuccessful rifle-range project for Madeira.

mentions.as_written: Carlos Roma Machado de Faria e Maia
mentions.note: Engineer of the Consultório de Engenharia who surveyed the 1895 city plan and made its reduction bought by the council in 1897.

mentions.as_written: Carlos Roma Machado de Faria e Maia
mentions.note: Engineering officer who taught as interim replacement for Nowach until 1897.

summary: Engineering officer who surveyed the 1895 plan of Funchal and in 1895–96 took part in bids for the Madeira levada concession. He also drew up an early, unsuccessful rifle-range project and taught at the Escola Industrial until 1897.

name: Manuel Madureira da Maia

mentions.note: One of Madeira's first settlers, living at Gaula.

summary: One of Madeira's first settlers, living at Gaula.

name: Adolfo Loureiro

mentions.note: Engineer quoted on how little was known about the tides and waters of the port of Funchal.
Engineer sent to study the water regime of Madeira, who left in April 1898 after recommending the adapted decree.
Author of Os Portos Marítimos de Portugal e Ilhas Adjacentes (1910).
Portuguese engineer, author of «Os Portos Marítimos de Portugal e Ilhas Adjacentes», quoted here on Madeira's currents, depths and tides.
Engineer quoted lamenting the lack of oceanographic study of Madeira's tides and waters.
Engineer whose work Portos Marítimos de Portugal supplied the 1909 fishing statistics quoted here.
Author of Os portos marítimos de Portugal, quoted on the Faial quay.
Author of 'Os Portos Maritimos de Portugal e Ilhas Adjacentes', with a detailed account of the Pontinha breakwater.
Engineer whose work 'Os Portos Marítimos de Portugal e Ilhas Adjacentes' (vol. 5) describes Madeira's ports in detail.
Portuguese engineer whose work Os Portos Maritimos de Portugal e Ilhas Adjacentes devotes its fifth volume to the Madeira archipelago.
Author of Os Portos Marítimos de Portugal e Ilhas Adjacentes (1910), cited as a source.
Engineer who studied Madeira's hydraulic regime in 1898 and devoted a volume of Os Portos Marítimos de Portugal to Madeiran ports.

summary: Portuguese engineer sent to Madeira in 1898 to study the application of the 1892 water regime. He wrote on the archipelago and its ports, devoting the fifth volume of Os Portos Marítimos de Portugal e Ilhas Adjacentes (1910) to Madeira.

name: João Marques Loureiro

mentions.note: Author of Estudos Ampelográficos (Lisbon 1912) describing Madeiran grape varieties.

summary: Author of Estudos Ampelográficos (Lisbon 1912) describing Madeiran grape varieties.

name: Henrique Franco de Sousa

mentions.note: Madeiran painter born in Funchal in 1883, trained at the Royal Academy of Fine Arts in Lisbon and a Valmor grant holder, who is the subject of this entry.
Interim teacher at the school.

summary: Funchal-born painter trained in Lisbon under Columbano Bordalo Pinheiro who studied in Madrid and Paris on the Valmor grant. He returned to Madeira in 1914 and taught as an interim teacher at the Escola Industrial.

name: Afonso Caminha de Vasconcelos e Sousa
aliases: Afonso Caminha de Vasconcelos e Sousa

mentions.as_written: José Caminha de Vasconcelos e Sousa
mentions.note: Last donatary of Funchal, who ceded his rights to the crown in 1766 in exchange for a marquessate and a pension.

mentions.as_written: José Caminha de Vasconcelos e Sousa
mentions.note: Last donatary of the captaincy of Funchal, who surrendered most of its rights to the Crown in 1766.

summary: Count of Calheta who received the captaincy of Funchal as its donatary in 1726. The notes also associate the name with the last donatary, who ceded the captaincy's rights to the Crown in 1766.

name: José Caminha de Vasconcelos e Sousa
aliases: Afonso Caminha de Vasconcelos e Sousa

mentions.note: Count of Calheta and donatary of Funchal, receiving the captaincy in 1726.

summary: Count of Calheta and donatary of Funchal, receiving the captaincy in 1726.

name: Gonçalo de Sousa

mentions.note: Judge of the Casa da Suplicação sent in 1614 to punish crimes in Madeira, without lasting effect.
Desembargador of the Casa da Suplicação sent in 1614 to judge maladministration and killings, though the accused fled.

summary: Desembargador of the Casa da Suplicação sent to Madeira in 1614 to judge maladministration and killings. His mission had no lasting effect, as the accused fled.

name: Francisco de Sousa

mentions.note: Pharmacist whose dispute with Dr. João da Camara Leme was the subject of pamphlets in 1868 and 1869.
Governor General of Madeira from 1627.
Madeiran royal factor in Funchal who wrote the Tratado das Ilhas Novas (1570).
Governor-general of Madeira appointed 18 January 1627, in office from 1 May 1628.
One of the parish priests of Caniço between 1538 and the end of the eighteenth century.
Funchal pharmacist, father of Francisco Clementino de Sousa, whom his son defended in an 1868 pamphlet.
First master gunner (condestável), appointed in 1624 on 24$ a year and two pipes of wine.
Secretary and pharmacy teacher after 1858.
Pharmacist named in the title of an 1869 pamphlet by Canavial.

summary: Madeiran-born royal factor in Funchal and author of the Tratado das Ilhas Novas (1570) on the New Islands and the settlement of Newfoundland, printed in Ponta Delgada in 1877 and 1884. The notes under this name also refer to other namesakes, including a governor-general from 1627 and a Funchal pharmacist.

name: Francisco Clementino de Sousa

mentions.note: Physician-surgeon to whom an anonymous 1868 pamphlet on the Camara Leme dispute is attributed.
One of the paper's successive editors.
Madeiran satirical poet said to descend from Medina.
One of the young co-authors of the satirical poem A Guyaneida.
Funchal physician and satirical poet, subject of this entry, who wrote under the pseudonym Faustino Brasão.
Graduate, twice interim professor and a distinguished alumnus.
Distinguished Madeiran writer and father of the geologist Francisco Luís Pereira de Sousa.

summary: Funchal-born physician, sanitary inspector and bank treasurer, best remembered as a gifted satirical poet and journalist who often wrote as 'Faustino Brasão'. He co-wrote A Guyaneida, edited the Diário de Notícias and was twice interim professor at the Escola Médico-Cirúrgica.

name: Manuel Alexandre de Sousa

mentions.note: Madeiran captain who won the 1896 levada concession, then had it rescinded in 1899 without having built anything.
Respondent in an 1896 appeal to the Lisbon court over the levadas enterprise.
Governor and captain-general who built the customs redoubt in 1645.
Madeiran captain who took over the concession in 1890 and directed the works until dismissed in 1893.
Infantry major, technical inspector of the Monte Railway Company and concessionary for levada works.

summary: Funchal-born infantry major who directed the Monte railway works from 1890 to 1893 and won the 1896 levada concession, which was rescinded in 1899. He was later director of the Limoeiro prison.

name: João Albino Rodrigues de Sousa

mentions.note: Co-contractor for the 1908–10 capture of the Tornos springs.
High diver who set a Portuguese record with a 25-metre dive into the sea.
Provedor present in 1521 when the patron was chosen.
Physician heading the Red Cross first-aid post in Funchal from its opening in early 1917.
Red Cross physician in Funchal who treated the wounded in 1917.

summary: Physician who headed the Red Cross first-aid post in Funchal from its opening in early 1917 and treated the wounded of the 1917 bombardment. The name also appears as co-contractor for the 1908–10 capture of the Tornos springs.

name: Cristóvão Falcão de Sousa

mentions.note: Governor General of Madeira from 1600.
Governor-general of the Madeira archipelago appointed in 1600, sometimes wrongly identified with, or said to be the son of, the author of Crisfal.

summary: Governor-general of the Madeira archipelago appointed in 1600. His link to the author of Crisfal is disputed.

name: Ernesto Venceslau de Sousa

mentions.note: Person to whom the name E. Tarolo refers.
Funchal typographer and poet who wrote the Poema antipuniceo (1904).

summary: Funchal-born typographer and writer, author of the Poema antipuniceo (1904). He contributed to local papers under the pseudonym E. Tarolo.

name: Bernardo Tavares de Sousa

mentions.note: Nobleman who settled in Madeira after 1580; another root of the Tavares family.

summary: Nobleman who settled in Madeira after 1580; another root of the Tavares family.

name: Maria Tavares de Sousa

mentions.note: Wife of João Portes Homem de El-Rei and co-founder of the Florenças chapel in 1684.
Wife of Simão de Nobrega e Sousa and co-founder of the Pico do Cardo chapel.
Mother of the 2nd Count of Castelo-Melhor.

summary: Noblewoman recorded as co-founder of the Florenças chapel in 1684 and of the Pico do Cardo chapel. She is also named as mother of the 2nd Count of Castelo-Melhor.

name: Justiniano Joaquim de Sousa

mentions.note: Skipper of the boat wrecked landing at Porto Santo in 1850.

summary: Skipper of the boat wrecked landing at Porto Santo in 1850.

name: Diogo Lopes de Sousa
roles: master of the Order of Christ

mentions.note: Prince Henry's predecessor as master, who left the Order prosperous.

summary: Prince Henry's predecessor as master, who left the Order prosperous.

name: José Xavier de Cerveira e Sousa

mentions.as_written: D. José X. Cerveira e Sousa
mentions.note: Bishop who blessed the cemetery chapel on 15 December 1844.

mentions.as_written: D. José Xavier Cerveira e Sousa
mentions.note: Bishop of Funchal 1844–1848, subject of this entry.

mentions.as_written: D. José Xavier de Cerveira e Sousa
mentions.note: Bishop of Funchal who recalled Andrade in 1844 to help oppose Protestant proselytism.

mentions.as_written: D. José Xavier Cerveira e Sousa
mentions.note: Twenty-second bishop of Funchal (1844–1848).

mentions.as_written: D. José Xavier de Cerveira e Sousa
mentions.note: Bishop of Funchal who sat on the asylum's first administrative committee in 1847.

summary: Coimbra theology professor who became bishop of Funchal (1843/44–1848) after a ten-year vacancy, during the period of Robert Kalley's Protestant proselytism. He was later bishop of Beja and Viseu.

name: Rui de Sousa

mentions.note: Nobleman of King João II's household who married Constança Cabral in Madeira, founding one Sousa branch.
Poet of the Madeiran group in the Cancioneiro de Resende.
Great-grandson of Diogo Cabral who rebuilt the chapel in 1560.
Cancioneiro poet married to a granddaughter of Zargo.

Governor of Porto Santo from 1805.

name: James Clark

name: F. A. Barral

summary: Portuguese physician and author of 'Noticia sobre o clima do Funchal', which is quoted at length in the Elucidário. He praised Bettencourt Pita's Account of the Island of Madeira and the water of the Fontes de João Diniz.

name: Francisco António Barral

mentions.note: Professor at the Lisbon Medical School who attended Princess Maria Amélia in Funchal and wrote on its climate.

summary: Lisbon physician and professor at the Lisbon Medical School who attended Princess Maria Amélia in Madeira in 1852–53. He helped found the Princess's hospice and wrote a valued study of Funchal's climate and tuberculosis.

name: Heberden

mentions.note: First physician to report favourably on Madeira's climate, in 1751.

Physician who was in Madeira in the 18th century and estimated average life expectancy on the island at 39 years.

Physician who recorded shade temperatures during the leste in 1750.

English physician resident in Funchal who assisted Banks and Solander.

summary: English physician resident in Funchal in the 18th century, the first to report favourably on Madeira's climate, in 1751. He recorded temperatures, magnetic declination and life expectancy on the island and assisted Banks and Solander during Cook's visit.

name: Thomas Heberden

mentions.note: Physician in Funchal who made Madeira's first meteorological observations and gave specimens to Banks and Solander.

summary: Thomas Heberden was an English physician in Funchal who served in the 1751 measles epidemic. He made the island's first weather observations (1747–51) and gave specimens to Banks and Solander.

name: William Heberden

summary: Well-known brother of Thomas Heberden.

name: Fothergill

summary: Dr Fothergill was a physician who wrote favourably on Madeira's climate. In his 1775 work on consumption he recommended it to people suffering from lung diseases.

name: Adams

mentions.note: Physician who wrote on Madeira's climate in 1801.
Physician who in 1802 asked the council for foundlings on whom to test smallpox vaccine and reported his results.

summary: Adams was a physician who wrote on Madeira's climate in 1801. In 1802 he asked the council for foundlings on whom to test smallpox vaccine, and he reported his results.

name: J. Adams

mentions.note: English physician who, according to the Elucidário, was apparently the first to vaccinate in Madeira, from 1802.

summary: J. Adams was an English physician who in 1802 obtained permission to vaccinate foundlings weekly. He was apparently the first doctor to apply vaccination in Madeira.

name: Gourlay

mentions.note: Physician whose 1811 work advised consumptives to winter in Funchal.
Measured Pico Ruivo in 1811 at 2,515 m, according to the Elucidário's table.

summary: Gourlay was a physician whose 1811 work advised consumptives to winter in Funchal. In 1811 he measured Pico Ruivo at 2,515 m.

name: William Gourlay

mentions.note: English physician who lived in Madeira from 1792 and published observations on its climate and diseases in 1811.

summary: William Gourlay was an English physician resident in Madeira from 1792 for 18 years. In 1811 he published a book on the island's natural history, climate and diseases, whose weather data were questioned.

name: Nicolau Caetano de Bettencourt Pita

mentions.note: Physician who wrote on Madeira's climate in 1812.
Editor of the Patriota Funchalense, condemned as a freemason in 1823.
Author of an 1812 work on Madeira's climate whose plate shows an earlier woollen cap.
Physician and editor of O Patriota Funchalense, banished for four years to Terceira, where he died in 1857.
Madeiran physician and ardent liberal who founded the Patriota Funchalense to promote constitutional principles.
Person whose main entry appears under 'Bettencourt Pita'.
Funchal-born Edinburgh-trained physician and liberal journalist who founded Madeira's first newspaper and died in exile-turned-residence in Angra.
Illustrious Madeiran cited as forgotten in Funchal street names.

summary: Nicolau Caetano de Bettencourt Pita (1788–1857) was a Funchal-born physician trained at Edinburgh. He wrote an 1812 account of Madeira's climate and founded the Patriota Funchalense, Madeira's first newspaper. A committed liberal, he was condemned in 1823 and exiled to Terceira, where he worked as a military and civil doctor until his death.

name: César Augusto Mourão Pita

mentions.note: Physician who wrote on Madeira's climate in 1859 and 1889.
Physician of the hospice for several decades until his death in 1907.
Physician, military surgeon and French consular agent in Madeira who wrote on the island's climate.
Deceased physician in whose estate the manuscript was found.

summary: César Augusto Mourão Pita was a Lisbon-born physician adopted as an infant by Dr António da Luz Pita. He wrote on Madeira's climate (1859, 1889) and was clinical director of the Hospício da Princesa Dona Maria Amélia in Funchal. He also served as a military surgeon and French consular agent.

name: Fortunato Alfredo Pita

mentions.note: Member of the medical commission favouring Santa Clara.
Funchal physician who wrote a 1923 article in Medicina Contemporânea on treating trachomatous conjunctivitis with heliotherapy.
Taught at the school.

summary: Fortunato Alfredo Pita was a Funchal physician who taught at the Medical-Surgical School and sat on a medical commission that favoured Santa Clara. In 1923 he wrote on treating trachomatous conjunctivitis with heliotherapy.

name: António da Luz Pita

mentions.note: Physician named in the title of Camara Leme's 1869 pamphlet on the medical school and the health delegation.
Notable Madeiran buried in the Angústias cemetery.
Madeiran physician who informed the Novara scientists in 1857.
Madeiran physician, died 1870.
Madeiran physician, first clinical director of the hospice and the Empress's agent in buying its land.
Helper of Empress Amélia in founding the Hospício alongside Andrade.
Distinguished physician who adopted César Augusto Mourão Pita as an infant when his family passed through Funchal.
Cabralist editor of O Archivista and A Ordem, later in the Popular party.
Madeiran physician presumed earlier owner of the copies.
Distinguished native of Ponta do Sol.
Madeiran physician and surgeon, deputy and health chief during the cholera epidemic; subject of this entry.
Madeiran writer whose periodicals Nóbrega also contributed to.
Madeiran physician and deputy who obtained relief from Lisbon during the 1856 cholera epidemic and organised clinical and hospital work on the island.
Replaced Lourenço Moniz as professor, presided over the first council and directed the school 1845–66.
Presided over the 1844 commission appointed to propose the creation of an asylum for beggars.
Madeira's delegate of the kingdom's health council and deputy, who brought government relief from Lisbon in 1856.
Physician named with Canavial as the two great medical figures of 19th-century Madeira.

summary: António da Luz Pita (1802–1870) was a Madeiran physician and surgeon from Ponta do Sol, trained in Montpellier and Paris. He served as health delegate, teacher at the Funchal Medical School and deputy in parliament, and led the medical response to the cholera epidemic. He was also the first clinical director of the Hospício da Princesa Dona Maria Amélia.

summary: Sentenced to five years' exile in Angola for the 1668 revolt.

Lawyer who was one of the editors and owners of the Revista de Direito (1920–21).
Author of a pamphlet on the expropriation of the Montado do Barreiro.

summary: Pedro Góis Pita (born 1891) was a Funchal-born lawyer and land registrar who served as deputy for Madeira and minister of Commerce and Labour. He wrote legal works, including a 1929 study of the Madeiran colonia contract.

summary: Carlos (Carl) Heineken was a physician who lived in Funchal for nine years. He recommended its climate for lung diseases and made valuable weather observations, and he died there in 1830.

summary: F. de Assis Sousa Vaz was a physician who published a treatise in Paris in 1832 praising Madeira's climate for treating pulmonary tuberculosis. He wrote it without visiting the island.

First donatary captain of Machico and ancestor of Vieira.

Co-commander of the discovery caravels with Zarco.
Captain-donatary of Machico, whose donation charter mentions the Infante's charter.
Captain-donatary of Machico, presumed also to have brought relatives and associates as settlers.

summary: Tristão Vaz was the companion of João Gonçalves Zargo in the discovery of Madeira and became first captain-donatary of Machico in 1440. The Elucidário argues that he never bore the surname Teixeira, which came to his descendants from his wife Branca Teixeira.

name: Salema Vaz

summary: Salema Vaz was a poet deported to Madeira in 1919 and held at the Gonçalo Aires lazaretto. His exile verses were published as Pão do Exílio in 1921.

summary: First known vicar of Porto Santo, apparently from 1572.

summary: Vicar of Estreito in 1539, the earliest recorded.

summary: Dr Kampfer was a German physician who stayed in Madeira in 1841 and 1842. He published 'Notizen über die Insel Madeira' in a medical journal in 1847.

summary: Robert White was an Englishman who lived in Madeira and wrote 'Madeira, its climate and scenery' (1851). He made meteorological observations in Funchal, Machico and Santo António da Serra.

name: White

Author of Madeira its climate and scenery, cited for 18 factories in 1856.
Author of 'Madeira its climate and scenery', whose second and third editions Johnson published.

summary: White was the author of 'Madeira its climate and scenery', cited for sugar-cane data and headwear. Its later editions were published by James Yate Johnson.

summary: Edward Vernon Harcourt was the author of 'A Sketch of Madeira' (London, 1850), which includes a list of Madeiran birds and meteorological notes. It also records four ox-driven cane mills in 1851.

name: Harcourt

Author who wrote on the vegetation of the Quinta da Palmeira.
Author of Sketch of Madeira, cited for four factories in 1851.

summary: Harcourt was the author of 'Sketch of Madeira', cited for four sugar factories in 1851 and for the vegetation of the Quinta da Palmeira. His list of Madeiran birds omitted the sparrowhawk.

name: W. V. Harcourt

summary: Author of meteorological notes included in 'A Sketch of Madeira'.

name: Francisco Maria dos Ramos

summary: Tondela-born dental surgeon who practised for many years in Funchal and was chief editor of the republican newspaper A Lucta. He addressed the crowd in Funchal at the proclamation of the Republic in October 1910. He later chaired political meetings in 1920 and 1923, the latter joining the Nationalist party.

name: Arnaldo de Azevedo Ramos

Early settler of Tábua.
One of the earliest priests of Gaula.

summary: Early settler of Tábua and one of the earliest priests of Gaula. He is also cited as a probable founder and leading board member of the Santa Cruz Misericórdia hospital.

name: Jacinto Fernandes

summary: Madeiran labourer and principal defendant sentenced to death by garrotte for the 1829 robbery and sacrilege in the Estreito de Câmara de Lobos church. The name also appears in a wall inscription as the donor of restoration work on the chapel of Santo André Avelino.

name: António Fernandes

summary: Sesmeiro at Covas do Faial and great-grandfather of João Fernandes Vieira, who took the name Fernandes from him. Namesakes include a co-founder of the Ribeira da Janela chapel (1630) and a bishop's nephew who helped calm the 1641 riot.

name: D. Olímpia Pio Fernandes

Madeiran woman author of plays.

summary: Madeiran woman writer, long resident away from the island, who contributed to newspapers. She wrote the drama 'Aldo ou a Filha do Mar', staged in Funchal around 1877 to great applause.

name: Manuel Joaquim Fernandes

summary: Parish priest of Santana from 1905, still serving in 1921, who had the church restored and its churchyard improved. A namesake murderer sentenced to death in 1855 is believed to be the last Madeiran so condemned.

He founded an entailed estate centred on his chapel of Nossa Senhora da Conceição at Arco da Calheta, where he is buried.

He was known for decades of popular science articles on medicine and hygiene in the Diário de Notícias, including a notable report on the 1919 influenza.

He was one of the twelve members at the first session of the Junta Geral in 1837.

Several species and the genus Monizia were named after him.

summary: So-called administrator of the Vera Cruz chapel, judged in 1587 not obliged to repair it.

summary: Recorded the hyacinth growing naturalised near Santa, in Porto Moniz.

summary: Director of the Diccionario Universal Portuguêz, to which Azevedo contributed articles.

summary: Royal physician resident in Funchal who wrote a life of Bishop Luís Figueiredo de Lemos, seventh bishop of Funchal, included in Frutuoso's history.

He was chiefly responsible for building the A.N.T. sanatorium in Madeira, which was named after him, and he gave unpaid help to the island's weather service. He died in Funchal on 14 June 1942.

name: José de Almada

His heirs owned the Quinta dos Tanquinhos.
Notary who wrote the Auto do Voto in 1523.

Named by some genealogies as an early bearer of the surname, who married Isabel Rodrigues Leal around the mid-16th century.
Co-author of an 1867 draft law regulating the colonia contract.
Person after whom the Pontinha road was once named an avenue.

summary: Dr José de Almada, born in Funchal in 1880, was a Coimbra-trained lawyer and senior official of the Portuguese Colonial and Foreign Ministries who undertook diplomatic missions abroad. In 1927 he came to Madeira to study the Lombada da Ponta do Sol question.

name: Pedro Álvares de Almada

mentions.note: Built the chapel in Santa Cruz in 1520.
Native of Guimarães and first Almada to come to Madeira; a leading officer of the Santa Cruz council said to have founded the church of Nossa Senhora da Graça there.
Noble early settler of Santa Cruz.

summary: Native of Guimarães and the first of the Almada family to come to Madeira. He was a noble early settler and a leading officer of the Santa Cruz council, and he built the chapel of Nossa Senhora da Graça there in 1520.

name: D. Lourenço de Almada

mentions.note: Governor and captain-general of Madeira (1688–90) who built the Varadouros gate and rebuilt the chapel above it in 1689.
Governor and captain-general of Madeira from 1688, later governor-general of Angola and of a Brazilian province; died 1729.

summary: D. Lourenço de Almada was governor and captain-general of Madeira, appointed in 1687. In 1689 he built the Varadouros gate and rebuilt the chapel above it. He was later governor-general of Angola and of a Brazilian province, and he died in 1729.

name: Margarida de Ornelas de Almada

mentions.as_written: D. Margarida de Ornelas de Almada
mentions.note: Mother of Dr José de Almada.

summary: Mother of Dr José de Almada.

summary: José António de Almada (1813–1885) was a Machico-born soldier who fled the Miguelist blockade of Madeira in 1832 to join the liberal forces. He was wounded at Asseiceira and decorated with the Order of the Tower and Sword.

name: Álvaro Vaz de Almada

mentions.note: Father of Pedro Álvares de Almada, the first of the family in Madeira.
Celebrated Count of Avranches, uncle of Pedro Álvares de Almada.
Ancestor of D. Lourenço de Almada.

summary: Celebrated Count of Avranches and ancestor of the Madeiran Almadas, including D. Lourenço de Almada. Genealogies make him either the father or the uncle of Pedro Álvares de Almada, the first of the family in Madeira.

name: António José de Sousa Almada

mentions.note: Madeiran poet of modest talent, civil governor of Castelo Branco under Saldanha's Hundred Days government, who died at Benfica.

summary: Madeiran-born minor poet and adventurer (1824–1874) who squandered a fortune. He served as civil governor of Castelo Branco under Saldanha's Hundred Days government and died at Benfica.

name: José António de Almada

mentions.note: Distinguished native of Machico.
Machico-born lawyer, civil governor of Funchal (1897–98) and deputy for Madeira in 1900; subject of this entry.

summary: José António de Almada (1843–1905) was a lawyer born in Machico. He served as civil governor of the Funchal district (1897–98) and as deputy for Madeira, securing several public improvements.

name: Francisco José Rodrigues de Almada

Young Regenerator politician.

summary: Surgeon who was appointed interim director of the Funchal asylum in 1906 and sat on the medical commission that favoured Santa Clara. He was also a young Regenerator politician.

name: Coelho Mendes

Azorean poet living in Funchal who published Flores Agrestes about 1885.

summary: Coelho Mendes was an Azorean resident of Funchal who published the poetry volume Flores Agrestes around 1884–85. He also wrote a reply to the newspaper A Verdade.

summary: Madeiran army staff major awarded the Legion of Honour and the British Distinguished Service Order.

summary: Machine-gun sergeant killed at Naulila.

summary: Chaplain of the hospice from 1908.

summary: Mother of João Fernandes Vieira, of the Lombada de Santa Cruz, and lawful wife of Francisco d'Ornelas.

name: Jerónimo Mendes

summary: Maternal grandfather of Vieira.

summary: Judge of Residues and Chapels in 1560.

Fourth bishop of Funchal (1556–1569).
Fourth bishop of Funchal and the first to take possession of the see in person, 52 years after its creation.

summary: D. Fr. Jorge de Lemos was a Dominican friar and the fourth bishop of Funchal (1558–1569), the first bishop to reside in person in the diocese. He reformed clerical abuses, reorganised the cathedral service and music, and oversaw the division of Funchal into parishes.

name: Maximiliano de Lemos

Editor of the Encyclopedia Portuguesa, cited on the origin of Calheta's name.

summary: Editor of the Encyclopedia Portuguesa Illustrada. The Elucidário cites him on Madeiran place names and on the African career of the Viscount of Cacongo.

summary: Governor and captain-general of Madeira, appointed in 1724, remembered for founding the Recolhimento das Órfãs in 1725 and for his work as provedor of the Misericórdia. He was succeeded by Mascarenhas in 1727.

summary: Last juiz de fora of Funchal, appointed in 1828 and serving until 14 June 1834. In May 1832 he went to Porto Santo to proclaim D. Miguel.

summary: Writer whose research on Vieira's parentage was confirmed by Sarmento.

Successor as governor of Madeira.
Governor who in 1804 recommended inoculation to all as the only effective defence against smallpox.

summary: Governor and captain-general of Madeira from 1803 to 1807, during whose rule the channelling and walling of Funchal's three streams was carried out. In 1804 he recommended smallpox inoculation to all.

name: Ascenso de Oliveira Freire

mentions.note: Governor of Madeira who in 1804 urged councils to afforest their municipalities and clean streams.

summary: Governor of Madeira who in 1804 urged councils to afforest their municipalities and clean streams.

summary: Scholar who praised A Insulana in his Arte Poética.

summary: Joaquim de Meneses e Ataíde (1765–1828) was an Augustinian friar and titular archbishop who was vicar capitular and governor of the diocese of Funchal from 1811 to 1821. He is remembered for his political quarrels with the captain-general and his services to the Funchal Misericórdia, including building the Angústias cemetery. He later became bishop of Elvas.

name: Ana de Mascarenhas e Ataíde

Wife of governor Mousinho de Albuquerque and active co-founder of the orphan asylum.

summary: Wife of Governor Mousinho de Albuquerque and an active co-founder of the Asilo da Infância orphan asylum in Funchal. On 14 January 1835 she presented a flag to the Funchal National Guard.

name: D. Luzia Maria da Silva e Ataíde

name: Luís Gonçalves de Ataíde

Son of Simão Gonçalves da Câmara who received the island as his mother's dowry.

summary: Son of Simão Gonçalves da Câmara, he received the Desertas as his mother's dowry and became their lord. He was captain of Ceuta and father of the Count of Atouguia.

name: João Gonçalves de Ataíde

summary: Sixth count of Atouguia, in whose house the Desertas were incorporated.

summary: Four times civil governor of Madeira between 1896 and 1910, the last effective civil governor under the monarchy, and deputy for Madeira (1908–10). He organised the grand reception for the royal visit of 1901 and died in Lisbon during the revolution of 14 May 1915.

Army captain and engineer who directed the District Public Works Directorate in Funchal.

summary: Artillery officer who commanded a garrison company in Madeira and was the first commander of its permanent artillery force (1877–78). He taught drawing at the Funchal lyceum, directed district public works, drew up the 1879–81 project for the new Funchal quay and wrote an improvement plan for the island (1879).

name: Domingos Alberto Cunha

summary: Director of Public Works in Funchal, defended in an 1860 pamphlet.

Funchal-born poet and humanist, author of O Espelho do Invisivel and secretary of the Junta dos Três Estados.
Poet and writer born in Funchal in 1654, son of the governor.

summary: Funchal-born poet, humanist and translator (1654–1729), son of Governor Bartolomeu de Vasconcelos da Cunha. He was the author of O Espelho do Invisivel and served as secretary of the Junta dos Três Estados.

name: Cosme Pais da Cunha

summary: Parish priest of Santana from 1672 to 1681.

summary: Captain-donatary of Graciosa and husband of Izeu Perestrelo.

summary: Suspended council clerk reinstated by the rioters in 1641.

mentions.note: Language teacher and journalist who was the association's first secretary.
Madeiran teacher and newspaper editor, imprisoned for a press offence in 1828, later professor of French and English in Funchal; died 1852.

summary: Liberal teacher and journalist who ran several Funchal newspapers, was jailed for a press offence in 1828 and went into exile. He later taught French and English at the Funchal lyceum, was the first secretary of the Associação Comercial do Funchal, and died in 1852.

name: Alexandre Luís da Cunha

mentions.note: One of the parish priests of Câmara de Lobos between 1570 and 1680.
One of the first teachers of the lyceum.
Teacher at the school whose departure for America in 1828 probably ended the Lancaster method there.

summary: Teacher at Funchal's Lancasterian school whose departure for America in 1828 probably ended the Lancaster method there. He was also one of the first teachers of the lyceum. The notes also record a Luís da Cunha among the parish priests of Câmara de Lobos between 1570 and 1680.

name: Pedro da Silva da Cunha

mentions.note: Governor and captain-general of Madeira, appointed 16 January 1655 and in office from 22 April 1655.

summary: Governor and captain-general of Madeira, appointed on 16 January 1655 and in office from 22 April 1655.

name: Martim Afonso da Cunha

mentions.note: One of Madeira's first settlers, holding sesmaria lands at Anjos and Canhas; founder of the Cunha family there.

summary: One of Madeira's first settlers, holding sesmaria lands at Anjos and Canhas; founder of the Cunha family there.

name: Augusto José da Cunha

mentions.note: Statesman who represented Madeira as deputy in the 1897–1899 legislature; died June 1919.

summary: Statesman who sat as deputy for Madeira in the 1897–1899 legislature. He died in June 1919.

name: Bartolomeu de Vasconcelos da Cunha

mentions.note: Governor and captain-general of Madeira appointed 1651, author of sonnets.
Governor and captain-general named in the 1654 inscription as builder of the Ilhéu fortress.

summary: Governor and captain-general of Madeira from 1651, named in a 1654 inscription as builder of the Ilhéu fortress. He also wrote sonnets and was the father of the poet Troilo de Vasconcelos da Cunha.

name: D. Pedro Alvares da Cunha

mentions.note: Governor and captain-general of Madeira appointed 1711, took office 1712.

summary: Governor and captain-general of Madeira, appointed in 1711 and in office from 1712.

name: João Severo da Cunha

summary: Funchal-born engineering colonel who was president of Lisbon city council under Pimenta de Castro. He was the author of technical works, including works on vaults.

name: Júlia da Cunha

mentions.note: Third wife of Francisco António da Câmara Leme, natural daughter of the Conde da Cunha; died of cholera in Lisbon in 1832.

summary: Third wife of Francisco António da Câmara Leme, natural daughter of the Conde da Cunha; died of cholera in Lisbon in 1832.

name: Conde da Cunha

summary: Father of D. Júlia da Cunha.

summary: Native of Calheta and earliest known parish priest of Santa Cruz, serving in 1538.

name: João da Câmara Leme Homem de Vasconcelos, Conde de Canavial

mentions.note: Head of the district in 1888 who studied the Misericórdia's administration and drafted a short-lived regulation.
Author of two 1885 pamphlets on sugar import duties and sugar-cane cultivation.
Titled noble buried in the Angústias cemetery.
Author of several works on Madeira wine and its treatment (1882-1900).
Madeiran notable who died in Funchal in 1902.
Madeiran who taught at the Funchal Medical School.
Nobleman who set up the short-lived white-mulberry nursery on the Praça da Rainha in Funchal.
Founded in 1889 an establishment using an improved wine-heating system described here.
Titled Madeiran who proposed an industrial bank in 1879 and 1886, without success.
Author of several works (1882–1900) on Madeira wine treatment.
Nobleman whose monument, moved from the Avenida do Doutor Manuel de Arriaga, stands in front of the dispensary.
Distinguished Madeiran honoured with a memorial.
Madeiran nobleman who, according to the Elucidário, sought to promote beetroot cultivation on the island for sugar production.
Madeiran promoter of sericulture who set up silkworm installations and mulberry plantations in Funchal in 1877.
Bought the theatre in 1887, after which it bore his title.

summary: João da Câmara Leme Homem de Vasconcelos, 1st Count of Canavial (1829–1902), was a Funchal physician, medical-school director, civil governor, journalist and industrialist who founded the Companhia Fabril de Açúcar Madeirense. He wrote widely on Madeira wine and sugar, and a bust to him was erected in Funchal in 1922.

name: Manuel Francisco Camacho

mentions.note: Canon who presided over the board that secured the Marmeleiros building for the hospital.
Canon who presided over the Misericórdia's governing board from 1930 to 1933 and was chiefly responsible for moving the hospital to Marmeleiros.
Liberal apparently from Santo António, where he died around 1880.

summary: Canon who presided over the governing board of the Funchal Misericórdia from 1930 to 1933. He was chiefly responsible for moving the hospital to the Marmeleiros building. The notes also record a Liberal of Mindelo named Manuel Camacho, apparently from Santo António, who died there around 1880.

name: Jorge Perestrelo Velosa Camacho

mentions.note: Lieutenant who worked on an early rifle-range project with Captain Eduardo Pereira.
Madeiran infantry captain decorated for African campaigns, monarchist, and Funchal official, assassinated in Lisbon in 1919.

summary: Funchal-born army officer (1870–1919) distinguished in Portuguese African campaigns. He was later a monarchist rebel, police commissioner and administrator of the Funchal municipality, and was murdered in Lisbon in 1919.

name: João Inocêncio Camacho

mentions.note: Madeiran journalist from Ribeira Brava who founded and chiefly edited the newspaper Religião e Progresso in Funchal (1879–1880).
Photographer who photographed the Columbus house window at its demolition.
Madeiran photographer who photographed the house.

summary: Journalist born in Ribeira Brava who died in Funchal in the last quarter of the nineteenth century. He founded and edited the Funchal newspaper Religião e Progresso (1879–1880) and, as a photographer, photographed the Columbus house window at its demolition.

name: Fernando Camacho

mentions.note: Man who served in the Spanish garrison in Madeira and, according to oral information cited by the annotator of the Saudades, may be the origin of the Camacho surname on the island.

summary: Man who served in the Spanish garrison in Madeira and, according to oral information cited by the annotator of the Saudades, may be the origin of the Camacho surname on the island.

name: Jacinto Augusto Camacho
roles: interim commander of the Madeira Military Division

mentions.note: Funchal-born Liberal officer who landed at Mindelo in 1832 and became a brigadier general in 1877.
Liberal who became brigadier-general and acting commander of the Madeira military division.
Colonel who served as interim commander of the Madeira Military Division between 1861 and 1868.

summary: Funchal-born Liberal soldier (1815–1885) who landed at Mindelo in 1832, fought in the civil war and rose to brigadier general in 1877. He served as interim commander of the Madeira Military Division between 1861 and 1868.

name: António Fernandes Camacho

mentions.note: Colonel and father of Jacinto Augusto Camacho.
Lieutenant-colonel among the refugees.
Artillery colonel and father of Januário Vicente Camacho.

summary: Artillery officer and father of Jacinto Augusto Camacho and Januário Vicente Camacho. As a lieutenant-colonel he was among the Liberal refugees aboard the corvette Alligator.

name: Henrique José Maria Camacho

mentions.note: Merchant who conceived the society, founded at his house in Rua da Bela Vista in 1862.
Madeiran Liberal who died at the Lisbon lines.

summary: Merchant who conceived the Associação de Socorros Mútuos 4 de Setembro de 1862, founded at his house in Rua da Bela Vista. The notes also record a Madeiran Liberal named José Camacho who died at the Lisbon lines.

name: Januário Vicente Camacho
roles: deputy and peer of the realm

mentions.note: Dean of Funchal Cathedral who came with the Liberals to Porto Santo.
Dean of Funchal Cathedral who fled with the liberals in 1828.
Dean of Funchal Cathedral and constitutionalist who came to Porto Santo aboard the frigate D. Maria II in 1832.
Great-uncle of Jorge Camacho; bishop-elect of Castelo Branco, deputy for Madeira and peer of the realm.
Dean who escaped the Miguelist occupation of 1828 aboard the Alligator.
Madeiran member of the Chamber of Peers.
Madeiran priest, dean of Funchal, diocesan governor of Funchal and Angra, deputy and peer, subject of this entry.
Madeiran governor of the diocese and bishop-elect of Castelo Branco who lent Castilho the Penha de França residence.

summary: Funchal-born priest (1792–1872) who became dean of Funchal Cathedral, bishop-elect of Castelo Branco, governor of the dioceses of Funchal and Angra, deputy for Madeira and peer of the realm. A Liberal, he fled the Miguelist occupation in 1828 aboard the Alligator and returned to Porto Santo with the constitutionalists in 1832.

name: Alexandre Fernandes Camacho

mentions.note: Second owner of the newspaper, after its founder.
Bought the Desertas in 1864; they later passed to his son of the same name.

summary: Second owner of the Diário de Notícias after its founder. He bought the Desertas in 1864, and they later passed to his son of the same name.

name: António Francisco da Cruz Camacho

mentions.note: Guarantor and inspector of the 1783–1789 church works, buried under its chancel arch.

summary: Guarantor and inspector of the 1783–1789 church works, buried under its chancel arch.

name: Brito Camacho

mentions.note: Minister who countersigned the decree of 11 March 1911 expropriating Madeira's brandy distilleries.
Leader of the Unionist party formed in 1911.

summary: Republican minister who countersigned the decree of 11 March 1911 expropriating Madeira's brandy distilleries. He led the Unionist party formed in 1911.

name: Augusto Maria Camacho

mentions.note: Colonel and genealogist, father of Jorge Camacho.

summary: Colonel and genealogist, father of Jorge Camacho.

summary: Mother of Jorge Camacho.

summary: Funchal bookbinder who learned photography in Paris and in 1864 opened Madeira's second photographic studio.

summary: Madeiran coal-barge worker killed when La Surprise sank in 1916.

mentions.note: Mother of Januário Vicente Camacho.

summary: Mother of Januário Vicente Camacho.

name: Carlos de Melo

mentions.note: Helped the board obtain the Marmeleiros building.
Author of 'Machico and the discovery of Madeira' in The Scottish Geographical Magazine, April 1896.

summary: Professor and author of 'Machico and the discovery of Madeira', published in The Scottish Geographical Magazine in April 1896. He also helped the Misericórdia board obtain the Marmeleiros building.

name: Florêncio José Correia de Melo

mentions.note: Governor and captain-general of Madeira who reported on Funchal's failed 1815 petition to absorb the rural Misericórdias.
Governor and captain-general of Madeira who had the Campo da Barca built and named it after the Conde da Barca.
Governor and captain-general of Madeira (1815–19) who reformed administration after the British occupation.
Governor and captain-general who took office in April 1815; the last name in Giraldes's list.
Governor and captain-general of Madeira, praised by the government in Rio for his reception of the archduchess.

summary: Governor and captain-general of Madeira from 1815 to 1819, who restored order and reformed administration after the British occupation and received Napoleon's passage and Princess Leopoldina. He had the Campo da Barca built and named it after the Conde da Barca.

name: Diogo de Azambuja de Melo

mentions.note: Governor General of Madeira from 1594.
Governor-general of Madeira under the Philippine monarchy, appointed 1594, installed 1595, died in Funchal 1600.

summary: Diogo de Azambuja de Melo was governor-general of Madeira under Philippine rule, appointed in 1594 and installed in 1595. He held office until his death in Funchal in 1600.

name: Januário Cardoso de Melo

mentions.note: The first and, according to the Elucidário, probably the only provedor do concelho of Funchal, appointed in 1834.
First provedor of the municipality of Funchal, who took office on 16 August 1834.

summary: Januário Cardoso de Melo was the first, and probably the only, provedor do concelho of Funchal. He was appointed in 1834 and took office on 16 August of that year.

name: Paulo Malheiro de Melo

mentions.note: Native of Viana do Castelo who settled in Madeira in the 18th century, founder of the present family.

summary: Native of Viana do Castelo who settled in Madeira in the 18th century, founder of the present family.

name: Patrício Malheiro de Melo

mentions.note: Funchal liberal in the 1821 revolt, member of the first constitutional Câmara and Prussian consul.
One of the twelve members at the 1837 first session.

summary: Patrício Malheiro de Melo (1791–1842) was a Funchal liberal active in the 1821 constitutional movement and a member of the first constitutional council. He was Prussian consul, fled the 1828 alçada, and sat among the twelve members at the first session of the Junta Geral in 1837.

name: D. Francisco Manuel de Melo

mentions.note: Seventeenth-century writer whose account of the discovery was studied by António Gonçalves Rodrigues.
Portuguese author of the Epanaphoras, to whose entry this heading refers the reader.
Writer and descendant of Zargo who said he was born at Matosinhos and first used guns on ships.
Writer descended from Zargo, quoted on his many titled descendants.
Writer whose third Epanaphora gives the most elegant version of the legend.
Portuguese writer, soldier and diplomat, author of the Epanaphoras, who popularised the Machim legend.
Author of the Epanaphoras de Varia Historia Portuguesa, criticised for erroneous references to these islets in the Machim story.
Portuguese writer, subject of Prestage's study.
Portuguese author cited regarding writers who poetically retold the Machim legend.
Portuguese writer who claimed to own the original manuscript of Alcoforado's account.
Portuguese author whose third «Epanafora» (1660), telling the Machim legend, was translated literally by Pavia.
Author of the Epanáforas who doubted the fire lasted seven years over the whole island.

summary: D. Francisco Manuel de Melo was a 17th-century Portuguese writer, soldier and diplomat descended from Zarco's line. His third Epanaphora popularised the Machim legend of Madeira's discovery. He stopped in Madeira in 1655 on his way to exile in Brazil.

name: António Maria de Fontes Pereira de Melo
aliases: António Maria Fontes Pereira de Melo
António Maria de Fontes Pereira de Melo

mentions.note: Prime minister who appointed Moniz Minister of the Navy in 1871.
Minister in Aguiar's government of 1867–68.

mentions.as_written: Antonio Maria Fontes Pereira de Melo
mentions.note: Regenerator head of government from late 1871, died 1887.
Leader of the Regenerator party, who showed Teixeira great esteem when he was a deputy.
Notable Portuguese statesman who, as a lieutenant of engineers, visited Madeira in 1858 and inspected the Rabaçal levada works.

summary: António Maria de Fontes Pereira de Melo was a notable Portuguese statesman and leader of the Regenerator party, who headed the government from late 1871 and died in 1887. As a lieutenant of engineers he visited Madeira in September 1858 and inspected the works on the Rabaçal levada.

name: Aleixo de Abreu de Melo

mentions.note: Doctor of medicine who served as physician to Philip III at the Spanish court.

summary: Aleixo de Abreu de Melo was a doctor of medicine who served as physician to Philip III at the Spanish court.

name: Sebastião José de Carvalho e Melo

mentions.note: Portuguese chief minister who appointed Sá Pereira governor.
Eighteenth-century Portuguese minister, named as the only government figure who did not neglect Porto Santo.

summary: Sebastião José de Carvalho e Melo was the 18th-century Portuguese chief minister who appointed João António de Sá Pereira governor of Madeira. He is named as the only government figure who did not neglect Porto Santo.

name: José Bandeira Coelho de Melo

mentions.note: Elected peer of the realm for Madeira in the 1894–95 session; died November 1897.

summary: José Bandeira Coelho de Melo represented Madeira as an elected peer of the realm in the 1894–95 parliamentary session. He died in November 1897.

name: Mário de Melo

mentions.note: Brazilian writer whose article, quoted here, defended Vieira's legitimate birth.

summary: Brazilian writer whose article, quoted here, defended Vieira's legitimate birth.

name: D. Rodrigo António de Melo

mentions.note: Governor and captain-general who laid the foundation stone of the Constitution monument on 28 January 1822.
Cathedral chapel master and composer of a Miserere and a work dedicated to Leo XIII.
Listed as a 19th-century Madeiran composer of sacred music.
Governor and captain-general of Madeira (1821–22).

summary: D. Rodrigo António de Melo governed Madeira as governor and captain-general from 1821 to 1822. He laid the foundation stone of the Constitution monument on 28 January 1822.

name: Martinho de Melo

mentions.note: Minister informed of the black-cherry measures.
Minister in Lisbon who corresponded with governor and bishop over their conflict.

summary: Martinho de Melo was a minister in Lisbon who corresponded with the governor and the bishop of Madeira over their conflict. He was also informed of the black-cherry measures concerning wine.

name: Melo

mentions.note: Early author who wrote the name as 'Machino'.

summary: Early author who wrote the name as 'Machino'.

name: José Maria Greenfield de Melo

mentions.note: Deputy for Madeira in 1890–1892.

summary: José Maria Greenfield de Melo was deputy elected for Madeira for the 1890–1892 legislature.

name: Francisco de Aragão e Melo

mentions.as_written: tenente de marinha Francisco de Aragão e Melo
mentions.note: Naval lieutenant commissioned by the Junta Agrícola in 1914 to carry out hydrographic studies of Porto do Moniz harbour.

summary: Naval lieutenant commissioned by the Junta Agrícola in 1914 to carry out hydrographic studies of Porto do Moniz harbour.

name: João Maria de Abreu Castelo Branco Cardoso e Melo

mentions.as_written: João Maria de Abreu Castelo Branco Cardoso e Melo
mentions.note: Portuguese nobleman, 1st Viscount and later 1st Count of Fornos de Algodres, appointed civil governor of the Funchal district in November 1852 and serving about a year.

summary: João Maria de Abreu Castelo Branco Cardoso e Melo (1789–1878) was a Portuguese nobleman, 1st Viscount and later 1st Count of Fornos de Algodres. He was appointed civil governor of the Funchal district in November 1852 and served for about a year.

name: Augusto Correia da Silva Melo

summary: Head of a government department (Repartição), named at the close of a document quoted in this entry.

summary: Mother of Henrique Henriques, through whom the Melo name entered the Câmara line.

name: D. António Jorge de Melo

mentions.note: Governor and captain-general of Madeira, appointed 13 March 1689 and installed 27 April 1689.

summary: D. António Jorge de Melo was governor and captain-general of Madeira. He was appointed on 13 March 1689 and installed on 27 April 1689.

name: Francisco Borges de Sousa e Melo

mentions.as_written: padre Francisco Borges de Sousa e Melo
mentions.note: Parish priest of São Vicente and its first archpriest (vigário da vara) from 1812.

summary: Parish priest of São Vicente and its first archpriest (vigário da vara) from 1812.

name: Pantaleão de Sá e Melo

Governor and captain-general of Madeira from 1694.

summary: Pantaleão de Sá e Melo was appointed governor and captain-general of Madeira on 1 March 1694 and took office on 22 July that year. He imprisoned three councillors during a Corpus Christi procession.

name: José Nosolini Pinto Osório da Silva Leão
key: jose nosolini pinto osorio silva leao

mentions.note: Civil governor who obtained funds for the hospital improvements inaugurated in 1940.

summary: Civil governor who obtained funds for the hospital improvements inaugurated in 1940.

summary: Genoese contractor of sugar duties in 1471–72.

Priest who described the 1923 pilgrimage in some twenty articles in A Esperança.

summary: Jacinto da Conceição Nunes was a priest who described the 1923 Madeiran pilgrimage in some twenty articles in A Esperança. As provedor of the Misericórdia he directed the 1940 improvements at Marmeleiros.

name: Abreu Nunes

mentions.note: Engineer colonel on the special rifle-range commission formed after 1904.

summary: Engineer colonel on the special rifle-range commission formed after 1904.

name: Filipa Nunes

Self-styled prophetess involved in the 1533 Porto Santo disturbances.
Seventeen-year-old paralysed niece of Fernão Nunes who joined his prophecies in 1533; later married and lived in Portugal.

summary: Filipa Nunes was the seventeen-year-old paralysed niece of Fernão Nunes, whose prophecies she joined in 1533. She was one of the self-styled prophets of the Porto Santo disturbances of that year, and later married and lived in Portugal.

name: Atanasio Herculano Nunes

mentions.note: Liberal veteran, Funchal customs employee, died in Santa Cruz in 1887.

summary: Liberal veteran, Funchal customs employee, died in Santa Cruz in 1887.

mentions.note: Father of João Pedro de Freitas Pereira Drumond.

name: Fernão Nunes

False prophet of Porto Santo, son of Bartolomeu Nunes, treated elsewhere in the Elucidário.
One of the early settlers of Porto da Cruz.
One of the 'prophets' of Porto Santo in the 1533 affair.
Self-styled prophet who incited the 1533 Porto Santo disturbances.
Impostor prophet in Porto Santo unmasked by the Moor Barque and then arrested.
Porto Santo man who in 1533 posed as a prophet for eighteen days, was arrested and sentenced to penance at Évora.

summary: Fernão Nunes is recorded as the first Nunes in Madeira, living in Gaula, married to Helena de Góis, and one of the early settlers of Porto da Cruz. A Fernão Nunes, son of Bartolomeu Nunes, was the false prophet of Porto Santo.

name: Bartolomeu Nunes

mentions.note: Porto Santo resident in the early 16th century, father of the false prophet Fernão Nunes.
Father of the prophet Fernão Nunes, living at Farrobo in northern Porto Santo.

summary: Bartolomeu Nunes was an early 16th-century resident of Porto Santo, living at Farrobo in the north of the island. He was the father of the false prophet Fernão Nunes.

name: Filipe José Nunes

mentions.note: Curate of the Sé parish and honorary canon, known for fierce journalism in O Popular.
Canon active in the Popular party.

summary: Filipe José Nunes (1824–c.1890) was a Madeiran priest, curate of the Sé parish and honorary canon. He was a combative journalist of O Popular and was active in the Popular party.

name: Padre Manuel Nunes

mentions.note: Parish priest of São Gonçalo, distinguished preacher and satirical poet.
Priest and bass singer.

summary: Padre Manuel Nunes (1848–1892) was parish priest of São Gonçalo, a noted preacher and a satirical poet. He was also known as a bass singer.

name: João Frederico Nunes

mentions.note: Canon and vicar capitular of Funchal, named governor of the bishopric by Barreto in December 1876.

summary: Canon and vicar capitular of Funchal, named governor of the bishopric by Barreto in December 1876.

name: Jácome Nunes

summary: One of the earliest known settlers of São Roque do Faial.

One of the resident curates of Jardim do Mar between 1837 and 1848.

summary: Francisco José Nunes was one of the resident curates of Jardim do Mar between 1837 and 1848. He then served as the first parish priest of São Roque do Faial from 1848 until his death there in 1865.

name: Diogo Nunes

mentions.note: One of the parish priests of Câmara de Lobos between 1570 and 1680.

summary: One of the parish priests of Câmara de Lobos between 1570 and 1680.

summary: Funchal physician, public-health administrator, journalist and noted solver of mathematical problems. He directed the Correio da Madeira and edited the Diário de Notícias, and was first administrator of the Campo da Barca disinfection station until retiring in 1919. He also had the Abra quay built in 1905 and bought the original tramway company's rolling stock in 1900, later passing it to the Monte Railway company.

Portuguese poet, brother of the naturalist Augusto Nobre.

summary: Portuguese poet, author of 'Só' and brother of the naturalist Augusto Nobre. He stayed in Funchal in 1898–99 seeking a cure for pulmonary tuberculosis and was disillusioned with the climate. The former Praça do Ribeiro Seco was renamed Largo de António Nobre in his memory.

summary: Porto-born zoologist and university professor, brother of the poet António Nobre, who published studies on the marine and land molluscs and the pilot whales of Madeira. In 1927 he visited his brother's former house at Boliqueme and pensioned his brother's old servant.

summary: British general who secured British rule in the Transvaal. He received a brilliant welcome when passing through Madeira on his way home on 26 December 1900.

summary: English botanist who carried out tree planting in Madeira in 1774.

summary: Portuguese portrait painter (born 1756), son of the painter Manuel Joaquim da Rocha. He came to Madeira in 1807 fleeing the French invasion, taught the royal drawing and painting class from 1810, left several canvases on the island and died in Funchal after 1821.

name: Manuel Joaquim da Rocha

name: Vitúrio Lopes Rocha

Madeiran who took a doctorate in mathematics at Coimbra.

summary: Funchal-born doctor of mathematics (born 1752) who taught for many years at the University of Coimbra and was a member of the Royal Academy of Sciences. He later sought the post of prefect of the public schools of Madeira.

Funchal priest and canon lawyer, dean of the cathedral and several times governor of the diocese, persecuted as a former freemason.
Notable member of the Funchal chapter.
Madeiran dean who baptised the future viscount in 1797.

summary: Funchal-born canon lawyer and priest (1747–1819) who became dean of Funchal Cathedral and several times governed the diocese. He was persecuted by Bishop D. José da Costa Torres as a former freemason, and his 1793 letter of complaint was later published in London in 1822.

summary: Irish-born English physician and naturalist (1660–1753) who stayed in Madeira from 21 to 23 October 1687. He described the island in his Voyage, published in London, noting armed merchants, violence and syphilis among the patients who consulted him.

name: Ovington

summary: Visitor to Madeira in 1689 who noted that many inhabitants went armed and carried swords, and that Madeirans dressed in black.

summary: English clergyman and traveller, chaplain to James II, whose 'A voyage to Suratt in the year 1689' (London, 1696) describes Madeira, including an incident in which sailors of his ship went missing in Funchal. The Elucidário regards his account as containing several falsehoods.

Governor and captain-general of Madeira who had the fortress rebuilt and enlarged in 1767 and brought fifty cannon from London.

summary: Governor and captain-general of Madeira (1759–67) who carried out the arrest and expulsion of the Jesuits under Pombal's orders and sequestered their property. He also had the Fortaleza de São Tiago rebuilt and enlarged in 1767, with fifty cannon brought from London, and in 1762 reported emigration to Lisbon caused by overpopulation.

summary: Tristão Teixeira, called 'das Damas' for his courtly verses to ladies, was the eldest son of the discoverer Tristão Vaz and second captain-donatary of Machico. Believed to be the poet in Resende's Cancioneiro Geral, he was summoned to Lisbon over complaints and cleared himself of a grave accusation. He is buried in the chapel of São João that he founded in Machico church.

name: Gérard Belloc

mentions.note: French scientist who studied tuna fishing at Madeira in 1923.

summary: French scientist who studied tuna fishing at Madeira in 1923.

name: James Hornell

summary: English zoologist who made ethnographic studies in Madeira in 1924.

name: Regniard (J.)

mentions.note: Pseudonym used by the author of the 1895 Funchal pamphlet 'No Laboratório. Psychologia e Pathologia Cerebral', whose identity remained unknown to many.

summary: J. Regniard was the pseudonym of the author of 'No Laboratório. Psychologia e Pathologia Cerebral', a pamphlet published in Funchal in 1895 that caused a great local sensation. The real author remained unknown to many.

name: Macaulay

mentions.note: Naturalist who interpreted the Piedade bodies as corals of the Alcyonidae family.

summary: Naturalist who interpreted the Piedade bodies as corals of the Alcyonidae family.
