English scientist who stayed in Madeira in 1839–40, wrote on its geography, geology and climate and edited The Stranger in Funchal.

summary: Dr James Macaulay was an English scientist who stayed in Madeira in 1839–40. He wrote on the island's physical geography, geology and climate, edited the short-lived English newspaper The Stranger, and wrote the text accompanying Picken's plates in 'Madeira illustrated'.

name: J. Macaulay

mentions.note: Cited as an author on Madeira's geological formation.

summary: Cited as an author on Madeira's geological formation.

name: Smith

Observer whose measurement of 1,573 m was published in the Irish Transactions.

summary: Smith was a geologist who held that the calcareous bodies of Piedade were casts formed in spaces once occupied by plants. A measurement of Pico Ruivo at 1,573 m attributed to him was published in the Irish Transactions.

name: James Smith

mentions.note: Author of a memoir on the geology of Madeira, translated into Portuguese by António Pedro de Azevedo.
Scottish geologist of Jordan Hill whose classification of Madeiran basalts into compact, vesicular and scoriaceous types is followed in this entry.
English geologist who visited Madeira about 1840 and wrote on its geology for the Geological Society.

summary: James Smith of Jordan Hill was a geologist who visited Madeira around 1840 and published a paper on its geology for the Geological Society, later translated into Portuguese by António Pedro de Azevedo. His classification of Madeiran basalts into compact, vesicular and scoriaceous types is followed by the Elucidário.

name: Christen Smith

summary: Norwegian botanist who accompanied Buch to Madeira in 1811.

name: J. Gray Smith

summary: Measured the peak in 1861 at 1,849 m.

name: Smith (Chetien)

mentions.note: Norwegian botanist, born October 1785 and died in the Congo on 21 September 1816, associated with Leopold von Buch.

summary: Christen Smith was a Norwegian botanist, born in October 1785, who was associated with Leopold von Buch. He died in the Congo on 21 September 1816.

name: Ricardo Carlos Smith

mentions.note: English horticulturist who founded an acclimatisation garden in Funchal and wrote on sorghum cultivation.

summary: Richard Charles Smith was an English horticulturist who founded an acclimatisation garden with a reading room in Funchal. He published a work on sorghum cultivation in 1858.

name: Piazzi Smith

summary: Professor who claimed the Spanish Armada's largest ships used Madeiran vinhático and til, a claim treated with reserve.

Foreign writer who in 1823 remarked that the Paul da Serra could be put to use.
Visitor in 1823 who noted how little sugar was then made in Madeira.
Visitor to Madeira in 1823 who found little sugar being made.
Author of 'Excursions in Madeira' (London, 1825), which cites Kirwan's weather data.
English naturalist who studied Madeira and Porto Santo in 1823; author of 'Excursions in Madeira and Porto Santo'.
English naturalist and traveller who measured the peak in 1823 and described an ascent in his book Excursions in Madeira and Porto Santo.

summary: Bowdich was a naturalist who visited Madeira in 1823 and wrote 'Excursions in Madeira' (London, 1825). He identified the fossil beds of Porto Santo as Tertiary, interpreted the Piedade bodies as a petrified forest, and noted how little sugar was then made in Madeira.

name: Duque da Terceira

mentions.note: Liberal commander of the forces sent to the Algarve in which Camacho served.

summary: Liberal commander of the forces sent to the Algarve in which Camacho served.

name: Hanon

summary: Carthaginian navigator whose Periplus some think may have passed the archipelago.

name: Platão

mentions.note: Greek philosopher who described Atlantis, of which Madeira might be a remnant.
Ancient Greek philosopher whose account is the original source of the Atlantis legend.

summary: Plato was the ancient Greek philosopher whose account is the original source of the Atlantis legend. Madeira has been suggested as a possible remnant of Atlantis.

name: M. d'Avezac

mentions.note: French geographer whose Iles de l'Afrique discusses the discovery legends.

summary: French geographer whose Iles de l'Afrique discusses the discovery legends.

name: Pascoal Avezac Macaya

mentions.note: Foreign writer wrongly credited with claiming a population on the Deserta.

summary: D'Avezac was a French geographer and historian whose work Iles d'Afrique gave a broad survey of the Madeira archipelago. The Elucidário judges it flawed in places but valuable; a translation appeared in the Diario do Comercio in 1909.

name: Visconde de Santarém

mentions.note: Historian who had dismissed the Spanish friar's voyage as of no historical value.
Published the Crónica da Guiné for the first time, in Paris in 1841.
Historian whose note attributes taller Portuguese town houses to abundant Madeiran timber.
Portuguese historian cited on the effect of Madeiran timber on naval and building construction.
Historian who commented that Madeiran timber changed Lisbon building styles.

summary: The Visconde de Santarém was a Portuguese historian who first published Azurara's Crónica da Guiné in Paris in 1841. He is cited on how abundant Madeiran timber influenced naval and building construction, including taller houses in Lisbon.

name: 2.º Visconde de Santarém

mentions.note: Portuguese scholar whose atlases and writings Freitas studied, compiled and annotated.

summary: Portuguese scholar whose atlases and writings Freitas studied, compiled and annotated.

Canon of Funchal Cathedral from 1572 and early historian of Madeira whose work informed Frutuoso.
Author of a Historia da Madeira who probably copied Cardoso's account.
Notable member of the Funchal chapter.
Canon of Funchal Cathedral whose 1579 account of the discovery of Madeira supplied Frutuoso's Book II.
Canon of Funchal cathedral who obtained a copy of the discovery account for Frutuoso.

summary: Jerónimo Dias Leite was a canon of Funchal Cathedral from 1572 and perhaps the first Madeiran historian. His history of the island's captains, based on Gonçalo Aires's account of the discovery, supplied Gaspar Frutuoso's Saudades da Terra.

name: Duarte Leite

mentions.note: Author of 1939 newspaper articles on who discovered Madeira.
Head of the Portuguese government in which Costa Ferreira served as minister of finance.

summary: Duarte Leite was head of a Portuguese government in which Costa Ferreira served as minister of finance. In 1939 he wrote newspaper articles on who discovered Madeira.

summary: Canon whose pamphlet passed with Vasconcelos's manuscript to another owner.

name: Manuel Gregório Pestana Júnior

Author of a study on the reconnaissance of the Madeira archipelago placing Cadamosto's voyages in 1449 and 1450.
Porto Santo-born lawyer, deputy for Madeira (1911–17) and Minister of Finance, author of works on sugar and on Columbus.
Author of O Reconhecimento do Arquipelago da Madeira (1920).
Administrator of the Funchal concelho who urged the mutinous troops to obey their officers on 7 October 1910.
Madeiran who served as a minister of state.
Author of Cristóbal Colom ou Simão Palha.
Lawyer and journalist whose 1920 pamphlet 'O Reconhecimento da Madeira' proposed a new date for the discovery.
Author of the pamphlet 'O problema sacarino da Madeira', published in Funchal.

President of the municipal administrative commission when the park's name was restored in 1913.

summary: Manuel Gregório Pestana Júnior (b. 1886) was a Porto Santo-born lawyer, deputy for Madeira (1911–17) and later Minister of Finance. As administrator of the Funchal concelho he urged mutinous troops to obey their officers on 7 October 1910. He wrote pamphlets on the sugar question, 'O Reconhecimento do Arquipelago da Madeira' (1920) proposing a new discovery date, and a study on Columbus.

name: Correia de Azevedo Júnior

mentions.note: Madeiran who took a medical doctorate at the Rio de Janeiro faculty of medicine and published his theses there in 1852.

summary: Correia de Azevedo Júnior was a Madeiran physician who took his doctorate at the Rio de Janeiro faculty of medicine, where he defended and published his theses in 1852.

name: António de Sousa Júnior

summary: Published in the Censo da metrópole the 1535 list of places sending procurators to the Cortes, which omits Madeira.

name: João José de Macedo Júnior

mentions.note: One of the paper's successive editors.

summary: One of the paper's successive editors.

summary: Francisco Gomes de Gouveia Júnior (1864–1926) was a retired postal officer, vice-president of Funchal council and head of the Misericórdia's commission. He was chief editor of the newspaper A Madeira (1897–1899).

name: João da Silva Júnior

summary: Reserve second lieutenant awarded the War Cross for service on 9 April 1918.

summary: Infantry second lieutenant decorated and captured at the battle of the Lys.

summary: Judge of the Funchal comarca from 1925, when the second court was added.

summary: José Teixeira Júnior (b. 1889) was a Funchal-born pharmacist at the Estefânia hospital in Lisbon. He wrote a pamphlet titled Em Lisboa.

name: Alexandre Fernandes Camacho Júnior

summary: Bought Bugio at auction after the Marquis of Castelo Melhor's death; his estate was auctioned in 1894.

name: Francisco Franco de Sousa Júnior

summary: Francisco Franco de Sousa Júnior (b. 1885) was a Funchal-born sculptor trained in Lisbon and Paris. His works in Madeira include monuments to the island's discoverer and to the victims of the 1916 torpedo attacks.

name: José Vieira da Luz Júnior

mentions.note: Head of the scouts' school for instructors on the first regional board.

summary: Head of the scouts' school for instructors on the first regional board.

name: João Fernandes Vieira
key: joao fernandes vieira francisco ornelas moniz junior

mentions.note: Madeiran-born leader of the Pernambuco revolt that expelled the Dutch from Brazil, later governor of Paraíba and Angola.

summary: João Fernandes Vieira (1596–1681), born Francisco de Ornelas Moniz in Machico, emigrated to Brazil. There he led the Pernambuco revolt that expelled the Dutch, and he later governed Paraíba and Angola. A monument to him stands in Funchal.

name: João Pestana Júnior

mentions.note: Madeiran poet and Coimbra law student who published Névoas de Lágrimas and died young in 1918.

summary: João Pestana Júnior was a young poet from Ponta do Pargo and author of Névoas de Lágrimas. He died in 1918 while a law student at Coimbra.

name: Manuel José Júlio Guerra Júnior

mentions.note: Funchal-born civil engineer without a completed degree, author of a Diccionario Topographico (1872) and a distinguished amateur photographer.

summary: Manuel José Júlio Guerra Júnior (b. 1845) was a Funchal-born practical civil engineer who did not complete a degree. He wrote a Diccionario Topographico for engineers (1872) and was a distinguished amateur photographer.

name: Francisco António Soares Júnior

mentions.note: Engineer who drew up a new Funchal harbour project, published in Lisbon in 1921.

summary: Engineer who drew up a new Funchal harbour project, published in Lisbon in 1921.

summary: Historian who wrote on Madeira as shown in fourteenth-century maps and portolans. He was co-author of Salvador Gonçalves Zarco (Cristóbal Colon).

name: Justiniano Lomelino de Serpa

mentions.note: Father of Pedro José Lomelino.

summary: Father of Pedro José Lomelino.

name: António Álvaro Dória

summary: Madeiran naval officer who served the Liberal cause. In command of the schooner Amélia, he brought news of the liberal victory to Madeira on 3 June 1834.

summary: Her heirs owned the Calheta chapel in 1921.

summary: Last capitão-mor of the Funchal captaincy, appointed in 1828, who was elected president of the Constitutional Municipal Commission in July 1834. A Luís Dória is also named by Frutuoso as the owner of a second sugar mill in Faial.

name: Luís Teixeira Doria

mentions.note: Owner of a second sugar mill in Faial, according to Frutuoso.

summary: Owner of a second sugar mill in Faial, according to Frutuoso.

Humble friar venerated as the 'Santo Servo de Deus', whose cult at São Bernardino was banned and his statue burned in 1835.
Franciscan lay brother venerated in Madeira as the 'Santo Servo de Deus'; he is the subject of this entry.
Franciscan friar known as the Santo Servo de Deus who lived in holiness at the São Bernardino convent.
Franciscan friar known as the Santo Servo de Deus, whose tomb at the convent drew pilgrims.
Friar associated with a religious legend of Câmara de Lobos.
Friar known as the 'Santo Servo de Deus', to whose entry this cross-reference points.

summary: Franciscan lay brother who died in the convent of São Bernardino at Câmara de Lobos in 1505 and was venerated in Madeira as the 'Santo Servo de Deus'. His tomb drew pilgrims and there were repeated attempts at his beatification. His cult was banned and his statue burned in 1835 by the diocesan governor.

name: Luiz da Guarda

mentions.note: Judge of Residues and Chapels in 1546.

summary: Judge of Residues and Chapels in 1546.

summary: Archdeacon of Funchal Cathedral who founded and endowed the Recolhimento do Bom Jesus from 1655.

name: Manuel Tomás

Seventeenth-century non-Madeiran poet who wrote A Insulana, a poem entirely about Madeira.
Author of the poem Insulana (Antwerp, 1635) about Madeira.
Poet from Guimarães and probably a canon of Funchal Cathedral; author of the epic A Insulana, murdered in 1665.
Poet and author of the Insulana, whose verses on the name Caniço are quoted here.
Author of the Insulana, which lists the Leitões among notable families.
Author of the Insulana, which praises João Bartolomeu in book X.
Author of the poem A Insulana, which praises Constantino de Caires.
Author of the poem Insulana, which mentions him.
Author of the poem 'Insulana', whose entry covers the work.
Author of the poem Insulana, who stated that cedar wood built Funchal's first two-storey house.
Author of the Insulana, which mentions melons among Madeira's fruits.
Named as the author of the poem A Insulana, which mentions Fernão Álvaro de Agrela.
Author of the poem Insulana, which names the Quintal surname.
Author of the poem Insulana, which praises the merits of Bartolomeu João.
Old writer whose account of an island-wide fire the Elucidário calls fantasy.

summary: Poet born in Guimarães who settled in Funchal, probably as a canon of the cathedral, and wrote the epic poem A Insulana (Antwerp, 1635) on the discovery and history of Madeira. He was murdered in 1665; the Elucidário questions the claim that his murder was linked to the ecclesiastical sedition of 1668.

name: Francisco Álvares de Nóbrega

Eighteenth-century Madeiran poet.
Madeiran poet who suffered in the 1792 persecution.
Madeiran poet to whose entry the article cross-refers in connection with the bishop.
Madeiran poet known as 'Camões Pequeno', the subject of this entry.
Poet known as Camões Pequeno, Machico's most illustrious son, born at Torre.
Madeiran poet known as 'Camões Pequeno', uncle of Januário de Nóbrega.
Madeiran poet imprisoned by the Inquisition, whose writings were largely destroyed by its familiars after his death.

summary: Machico-born poet nicknamed 'Camões Pequeno', persecuted by Bishop José da Costa Torres and imprisoned by the Inquisition, who took his own life in Lisbon in 1806. He is remembered chiefly for his sonnets, published as the Rimas in 1804.

name: Januário Justiniano de Nóbrega

Madeiran writer whose historical-statistical work paid for by Funchal council was lost.
Former Regenerator in the Popular party.

Funchal clerk, journalist and poet who is the subject of this entry.
Madeiran poet whose verse was meant to fill the unpublished second part of Flores Agrestes.
Author of an 1867 pamphlet on the empress's visit to Madeira and the founding of the hospice.

summary: Funchal municipal clerk, journalist and poet, nephew of the poet Francisco Álvares de Nóbrega, whose Rimas he reprinted in Funchal in 1850. He wrote an account of the Empress of Brazil's visit to Madeira and destroyed his collected poems shortly before his probable suicide.

name: Ciríaco de Brito e Nóbrega

Funchal-born journalist, editor at the Diário de Notícias in 1923, author and finance-department official.
Member of the Executive Committee.
Author of the book describing the 1901 royal visit to the archipelago.
Editor of the periodical As Faiscas in 1883.

summary: Funchal-born veteran journalist, translator and author, and civil servant of the district finance department. He was an editor of the Diário de Notícias and of As Faiscas, and wrote the book on the 1901 royal visit to the archipelago.

name: Alfredo de França Dória Nóbrega

mentions.note: Reserve second lieutenant awarded the War Cross and made a knight of Christ.

summary: Reserve second lieutenant awarded the War Cross and made a knight of Christ.

summary: Canon and archdeacon of Funchal cathedral, probably the holder of Vasconcelos's lost manuscript.

summary: Ouvidor and lieutenant of the fifth captain-donatary, possibly the founder of another branch of the Nóbrega family. In 1538 he joined in the decision to abolish the plague guards.

summary: Priest from Caniço who founded the chapel of Nossa Senhora da Esperança at Vale Formoso in 1744.

name: Jerónimo de Nóbrega

summary: Priest born in Caniço who made a fortune in North America and sent large sums to Madeiran charities and rich furnishings to his home church.

name: João António de Nóbrega

summary: Madeiran emigrant from Monte parish who settled in Georgetown, British Guiana. He took the initiative in founding the first Catholic church there, dedicated to the Sacred Heart of Jesus, and died in Georgetown in 1912.

name: Domingos de Nobrega

mentions.note: The poet's father, named in his seminary enrolment record.

summary: The poet's father, named in his seminary enrolment record.

name: Simão de Nóbrega

summary: Founder of the Nóbrega family in Madeira and of the chapel of Santa Quitéria in Santo António parish.

summary: Pharmacist who published 'The Cultivation of Cochineal' in the Pharmaceutic Journal in 1849.

Engineer and brigadier who directed the walling of Funchal's three streams in 1804–05.

Brigadier honoured by the street name for his public works in Madeira.
Brigadier sent in 1804 to channel Funchal's three streams after the 1803 flood; a street is named after him.
Brigadier and military engineer who distinguished himself in charge of the fortifications after 1756.

summary: Brigadier sent from Lisbon after the great flood of 1803 to direct public works in Madeira, notably the walls of Funchal's three streams from 1804. He also mapped the city and began the general map of the island. He died in Funchal in 1807 and a street is named after him.

name: Vicência do Carmo Oudinot

summary: Oudinot's widow, granted the chapel endowment of Felipe de Barros in reward for his services.

Nineteenth bishop of Funchal (1797–1810).
Successor to Bishop Torres, who protected the poet and had him freed from the Limoeiro prison.

Bishop of Funchal involved in serious disputes with governor José Manuel da Câmara.
Bishop of Funchal who with the chapter resolved in 1803 to hold an annual votive procession after the great flood.
Bishop who requested the curacy created in 1801.
Bishop of Funchal who protested that the chapel was demolished without his authorisation.
Bishop of Funchal exiled by the governor to Santo da Serra and accused of freemasonry, later kept in office.
Bishop who demanded the college back for the seminary and won the 1803 dispute with the governor.
Bishop who spent some months exiled in the parish by order of the governor.

José Manuel da Câmara, which led to his temporary expulsion from Funchal in 1803 and the governor's dismissal. After the 1803 flood he instituted the annual votive procession, and he protected the poet Francisco Álvares de Nóbrega.
